clue.text: TT again?

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time, so two Ts side by side picture one time following another

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about whether the Isle of Man motorbike races, the TT, are being held once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a picture: TT shows T (time) written after T, which read out is the phrase meaning repeatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means repeatedly, over and over, which is a fuller way of saying once more.

clue.text: Naive genius upset about Greek character with nothing

indicators.note: about means going around, so the rearranged letters surround the next pieces
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of genius are rearranged

parts.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
nothing is zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A simple-minded clever person is upset over a Greek letter and some zero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles genius to INGEUS, and 'about' wraps that round the Greek letter and the zero, which sit in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone innocent and unsuspecting, with a trusting lack of guile.

clue.text: Judge in year one gets up to have a good time

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means rising, so the assembled letters are read from bottom to top
in places the judge's letter inside the year-and-one letters

parts.note: taken as the word itself, spelt out
J is the abbreviation for judge, as in legal citations

explanation.surface: A judge, after a year, rises to celebrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts J inside Y + ONE to give YOJNE; 'gets up' reverses it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish or take pleasure in things is to have fun, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Something amusing, with noise and gaiety initially supplying cash

parts.note: fun is something enjoyable or entertaining
a din is a loud noise

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of gaiety is taken

explanation.surface: Entertainment, racket and merriment are what the sponsors are paying for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes just the G of gaiety.
explanation.definitionFit: Funding is money provided for a purpose, the act of financing.

clue.text: Trap of wire ran sneakily back

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A snare made of wire that was laid stealthily behind something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' marks the hidden run: wirE RAN SNEakily gives ERANSNE, which 'back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch in a snare or net is to trap, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Flier visits gallery about four to smarten up

parts.note: a tit is a small bird, something that flies

indicators.note: about means around, so the gallery's name goes around the numeral

parts.note: the Tate is a famous art gallery in London
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A bird drops in on an art gallery to spruce itself up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the gallery round the Roman numeral, giving TIVATE; 'visits' just joins the bird to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To titivate is to make small improvements to one's appearance, to spruce oneself up.

clue.text: I wander up to find person from New Zealand

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to roam is to wander

explanation.surface: Someone says they will travel to visit a New Zealander.
explanation.walkthrough: I + ROAM read upwards in the down entry spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the indigenous Polynesian people of New Zealand.

clue.text: Plain card to be had at a lower price

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person, a character
for less means cheaper, so less stands for a lower price

explanation.surface: An ordinary greetings card is to be sold off cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' looks like a playing or greetings card but means an eccentric person; 'to be had' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something characterless is dull and without distinctive features, which is what plain means here.

clue.text: Pub ale, machine brewed, perfect

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients together, so these letters are combined in a new order

explanation.surface: Beer from a pub made by a machine turns out flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' rearranges PUB ALE MACHINE, all thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Unimpeachable means beyond reproach or criticism, so flawless.

clue.text: Japanese leader colours 24 after rotten boisterous play

indicators.note: after says the leader and colours come behind the word for rotten

parts.note: meat that has gone off is said to be high, so rotten means high

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: inks are coloured dyes, so colours stands for inks

explanation.surface: A Japanese chief colours in a picture of decayed rowdy fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes J from Japanese; HIGH (gone off, of meat) comes first because the rest is 'after' it.
explanation.definitionFit: High jinks is lively, rowdy fun and horseplay.

clue.text: Sharp projection lookout finally observed on Cape

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter of lookout is used

parts.note: Cape Horn is the southern tip of South America, so Cape gives horn

explanation.surface: A lookout on a ship sees a sharp headland as he rounds the cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the T of lookout; 'observed on' joins it in front of HORN.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a sharp spike growing on a stem, a pointed outgrowth.

clue.text: Not set to escape to New York

parts.note: to run is to flee or escape

explanation.surface: A fugitive, not settled anywhere, flees to New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not set' is the definition: jelly or a sauce that has not set is still liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something runny is liquid or soft rather than firm, the way unset jelly is.

clue.text: Roman idiom? Claim it is badly translated

indicators.note: a bad translation scrambles the original, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a Latin saying has been rendered wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman' here means Italian, not Latin; 'badly translated' rearranges CLAIM IT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian word or idiom used in another language is an italicism, and Rome is Italy's capital.

clue.text: Finish Conservative going 2 down to defeat

parts.note: a side going down to defeat is losing

explanation.surface: A political sentence about a Tory whose career ends in electoral defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Closing is the concluding part of something, its end.

clue.text: Belonging to a particular class worker becomes a grass

parts.note: in form means in a school class, a form being a class in British schools
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A member of a certain social class becomes a police informer.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a class is a 'form', so 'in form' means belonging to one; 'grass' is British slang for someone who informs to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a grass is someone who tells tales to the police, a snitch.

clue.text: Time certain to achieve this removal

parts.note: an era is a period of time
sure means certain

explanation.surface: With time and confidence you can get rid of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to achieve this' links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An erasure is the act of rubbing out or deleting, a removal.

clue.text: Filing put off is raising the spirit

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Postponing paperwork lifts one's mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges FILING PUT; 'is' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uplifting is inspiring and cheering, lifting one's mood.

clue.text: Relaxing by sea having resolved fuel crisis

indicators.note: resolved means broken up and worked out again, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Life by the sea is calm once the fuel shortage has been sorted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' rearranges SEA and FUEL together; 'crisis' is surface padding pointing the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Easeful is an old literary word for comfortable and soothing, as in restful.

clue.text: Instrument containing clear crescent-shaped space

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the instrument's letters enclose the next word

parts.note: a lute is a stringed musical instrument
to net a sum is to clear it as profit after expenses

explanation.surface: A musical instrument has a clear half-moon opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear' looks like an adjective describing the space, but is the verb meaning to make as profit; 'containing' puts it inside the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunette is a half-moon shaped area, as in an arched window or wall space.

clue.text: Varnish shown in petrol account

parts.note: Shell is a well-known petrol company with filling stations

explanation.surface: A coating seen on the books of a fuel company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown in' links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin dissolved in alcohol and used as a wood finish.

clue.text: Unproductive trees planted haphazardly around one on left

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the next pieces
planting trees without order scatters them, so the letters of trees are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Trees put in at random around a lone tree on the left side fail to bear fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planted haphazardly' makes STERE from TREES, and 'around' wraps it round I + L ('one on left').
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile land or animals produce nothing, so it means barren, without yield.

clue.text: Pine mountains at a great 5 distance

parts.note: to pine for something is to long for it
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: Pine-covered mountains seen far away on the horizon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the tree but is the verb to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-range describes something that covers or reaches across a far span, such as a missile.

clue.text: Innocent one seen in part of church

indicators.note: seen in means appearing inside, so one's letter goes inside the church part

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A guileless person is spotted in the main aisle of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means unworldly and trusting, lacking experience.

clue.text: Judge a pair of fellows 6 found with a citrus fruit

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow, so two fellows give two Fs

explanation.surface: A judge and two men are caught holding an orange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaffa is a variety of sweet orange, named after the port near Tel Aviv.

clue.text: Architect from Indiana

explanation.definitionFit: Inigo Jones was the English architect of the Banqueting House, and Indiana Jones is the film adventurer.

clue.text: One Hindus worship quietly taking heart from rival

parts.note: sh is the sound used to ask for quiet

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so all but the first and last letters of rival are taken

explanation.surface: A Hindu devotee quietly gains courage from a competitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart from' takes the middle three letters of rival; 'taking' joins them after the call for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiva is one of the principal gods of Hinduism, the destroyer.

clue.text: Nine involved in court case every three years

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the court case

parts.note: a trial is a case heard in court

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of nine are jumbled

explanation.surface: Nine people are caught up in a lawsuit that comes round once every three years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles nine to ENNI, and 'in' puts that inside the court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Triennial describes something happening once in each three-year period.

clue.text: Catch soldiers eating together with time to understand

parts.note: to catch a meaning is to get it
a military mess is where soldiers take meals together, so the phrase gives the mess
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Grab troops who are having dinner, and do it in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' links the pieces; 'the mess' is the place, or the group, of service personnel dining together.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp a hint or meaning is to comprehend it, the idiom for catching on.
